children: Copper prices fall to their lowest levels since late July as investors are worried that a Democratic sweep in the U.S. midterm elections could threaten the rapid expansion of artificial-intelligence infrastructure and lower the risk of import tariffs. Three-month copper futures on the LME are down 0.2% to $13,745 a metric ton--on track for a weekly loss of nearly 3%--amid a broader tech selloff driven by concerns over tighter AI regulation. Still, the longer-term supply outlook remains supportive, analysts say, citing tight physical availability, declining inventories in China and disruptions to global mine production. "Copper is experiencing a significant disconnect between tightening physical supply and weakening financial market confidence," says Zaye Capital Markets' Naeem Aslam. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
